_comment: EXAMPLE config for the Clairvoyance Versioning Backup System. Copy to config.json, replace every <PLACEHOLDER> and example path with your interview values, and delete the _comment* keys (the engine ignores unknown keys; these are annotations only). All paths are Windows paths with escaped backslashes.
_comment_instanceName: Destination subfolder name for this machine. Default to the PC hostname; use a nickname if multiple Clairvoyance installs share one PC.
_comment_backupRoot: Destination root. A UNC share (\\server\share\...) or a local/second-disk path (e.g. D:\Backups\Clairvoyance). Per-instance tiers are created under <backupRoot>\<instanceName>\.
_comment_copyMethod: robocopy (default, needs elevation for /B open-file copy) | vss | appclose | tar.
_comment_toolDir: <TOOL_DIR> is the permanent local fixed-disk tool directory chosen in Step 5a. stagingDir holds the persistent robocopy mirror (needs room for ~one uncompressed daily set); it may point at a roomier disk instead of <TOOL_DIR> if needed.
_comment_abortAfterLocalTime: Guard: a real (non -RunDate) run aborts if it is still running past the NEXT occurrence of this local time on/after the run's start, to avoid overrunning a reboot/maintenance window. A 03:00 nightly gets a ~45min deadline; an off-hours run rolls to the next day's cutoff instead of aborting instantly. Set just before that window.
_comment_minAbortWindowMinutes: Floor for the abort-window deadline (default 20 if omitted). If the computed deadline is within this many minutes of the run's start, it rolls to the next day instead — so a late-starting nightly (machine asleep -> Task Scheduler catch-up near the cutoff) runs to completion rather than aborting mid-run and producing no backup that night. Set a bit above a typical delta run's secrets+compress time.
_comment_deepVerifySample: How many random files to extract FROM the destination archive and hash-check after upload.
_comment_secretScanMaxFileKB: Files larger than this are NOT scanned and therefore NOT scrubbed; the run still reports ok=true. This is a deliberate cost cap, not a guarantee — 'no secrets found' and 'nothing was examined' produce the same green. The scan-counts ledger below exists precisely so that the size of this blind spot is visible instead of implied.
_comment_secretScanAuditRate: Fraction of files skipped by the incremental scan that are re-read each run to check their stored verdict is still right. Setting this to 0 disables REUSE, not the audit: with no audit, nothing can falsify a stored verdict, so reuse becomes unfalsifiable and the run reads every file instead. 0 therefore means MORE work, not less. OMIT THIS KEY to accept the built-in default, which is the value shown here.
_comment_secretScanDelta: Coverage-drift assert over 'secret-scan-counts.jsonl' (written next to lastRunFile, one line per run). Two checks: a per-run DELTA against the previous Live run, and a LEVEL check against the best coverage in the last anchorWindow Live runs — the level check is what makes a slow night-by-night ratchet downward impossible. Verdict is WARN-only and never sets ok=false. OMIT THIS KEY ENTIRELY to accept the built-in defaults, which are exactly the values shown here.
_comment_secretScanDelta_provisional: THESE DEFAULTS ARE PROVISIONAL, NOT EMPIRICAL. They were sized on the origin system from three nightly rows plus one read-only baseline, and the code says so at the point of definition. They are a starting point for YOUR churn, not a tuned recommendation: expect to widen them if your first weeks produce WARNs on ordinary activity, and to narrow them once you have real variance data. A band nobody has calibrated is a band that trains you to ignore it.
_comment_secretsCredentialName: Fallback: name of an environment variable holding the AES passphrase if the DPAPI passphraseFile is absent. The DPAPI-sealed passphraseFile is the primary mechanism (Step 7).
_comment_protectedPaths: Staff-continuity assertion. Each glob (PowerShell -like, case-insensitive; '*' spans any characters including '/') is matched against '<source>/<rel>' of the combined manifest; each must have >=1 file in the archive, else the run logs a FAIL stage and sets ok=false (loud, but does NOT abort — you still get that night's backup). This guards the Staff-member files (definition profiles/staff.json, history agent-sessions.json, custom personas, and the Home workspace's .Clairvoyance/staff memory) against being silently dropped by a future exclude. Per-workspace staff memory is reported (not required) since not every workspace has it; add 'workspace-<Name>/.Clairvoyance/staff/*' to hard-require a specific workspace. Omit this key entirely to disable the check.
_comment_staffMemory: F17 staff-memory coverage drift. staffMemoryProjectsRoot is where per-workspace agent memory directories live; the run asserts the configured staff-memory sources still match what is actually on disk, in BOTH directions, and sets ok=false on drift (which under the promotion guard withholds Weekly/Monthly/Annual). staffMemoryIgnore lists derived directory slugs that are deliberately NOT backed up.
_comment_staffMemory_coupled: THESE TWO KEYS ACTIVATE TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL. Setting staffMemoryProjectsRoot without staffMemoryIgnore is destructive in a quiet way: any unconfigured directory under the root reads as drift, so the check fires ok=false on run one and every run after, and a permanently-failing check is one nobody reads. Omit BOTH keys to disable, or set BOTH. The read-only scripts/Invoke-StaffMemoryCoverageCheck.ps1 reports the same comparison WITHOUT touching ok, and is the safe way to see what would fire before you enable this.
_comment_clairvoyanceExePath: App-version source for the backup version-stamp and the restore-time mismatch warning. Read as file metadata (FileVersion, then ProductVersion) at backup time into BACKUP-META.json and compared at restore time. Point this at the INSTALL directory deliberately: it is independent of wherever the user-data base directory lives, so relocating your data does not invalidate the stamp. If unresolvable, backups stamp 'unknown' and WARN — they never abort on it.
_comment_retention: How many of each tier to keep. -1 = keep all. Weekly slot = lastDayOfWeek; monthly = month-end; annual = year-end.
_comment_secretsRetention: Shorter prune schedule applied to the encrypted *_secrets archives.
_comment_sources: Non-workspace source roots. The home-appdata excludeDirs above are the standard Electron caches (safe to keep as-is). Add/remove dependency entries as needed.
_comment_workspaceDefaults: Applied to every auto-discovered workspace unless overridden in workspaceTuning. artifactDirs are routed to the weekly incremental Artifacts tier instead of the daily set.
_comment_workspaceTuning: Per-workspace overrides, keyed by workspace folder name. Exclude regenerable dirs (venv/.venv/site-packages, model blobs, node_modules, downloads) from the daily set. encrypt=true (F6a) routes that workspace's daily files into the AES-256 _secrets.7z instead of the plaintext _main.7z. WARNING: encrypting a workspace means losing the passphrase makes it unrecoverable — default false; only encrypt genuinely sensitive workspaces.
_comment_secretsSet: Files/dirs always routed to the encrypted archive and excluded from the plaintext main archive. Match-Secret (F7) is depth-agnostic: a bare filename matches at any depth; dir/** matches that directory anywhere. Confirm/add during interview Step 9.
_comment_secretScanPatterns: Regexes the pre-compress leak scan (F7) warns on if matched inside the plaintext set. Extend for your own token shapes.
_comment_orchestrators: Staff that run automated pipelines and must pause during backup (Step 8 / §9a). pauseCompliance: unverified | compliant | noncompliant. Empty array is fine if none.
